To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the u-boot gene regulates the choice of muscle precursor cells to adopt slow versus myogenic switch that specifies slow fiber development in zebrafish muscle precursors.

the u-boot gene is a myogenic switch in zebrafish that controls the choice of myogenic cells to adopt slow versus fiber developmental pathways, that the homeobox gene, prox1, functions as a downstream target of u-boot in this developmental program and that prox1 regulates slow myofibrils assembly.
u-boot is required for the specification of slow myoblasts and that prox1 is required for the differentiation of slow muscle cells in the zebrabish embryo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that govern the formation of skeletal muscle in vertebrates.
how the vertebrate embryo generates the diversity of muscle cell types that underlie the functional properties of skeletal muscles.
understanding the molecular and genetic basis of vertebrate muscle diversification and evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

u-boot is a gene that is required for the development of slow muscle fibres in the trunk of zebrafish embryos, and that this requirement is due to a failure to activate the slow myogenic program in u-boot mutant embryos.
U-Boot is a myogenic switch for slow muscle fiber specification in the embryonic zebrafish.
the u-boot gene is required in the slow myotome for prox1 activation and that this is a prerequisite for slow muscle differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified u-boot as a gene that is necessary to establish slow myofibers in the zebfish embryo.
the u-boot gene is essential for slow muscle fiber differentiation in zebrafish embryos.
we have shown the genetic regulation of slow versus fast muscle diversification and the genetic control of myofibrillogenesis in the zebrafish embryo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single gene, u-boot, can act as a switch to control whether myoblasts differentiate into slow or fast fibers.
the Hedgehog signaling pathway is required in slow muscle precursors to maintain their slow fiber fate.
the genetic programs that control the diversification of distinct types of skeletal muscle in vertebrate embryos can be remarkably specific.
